Messages.Author: Adam Hattrell
Messages.Body:
Here are a few questions that came up in a recent game. A ruling
would be nice...

(i) If range in combat is set to long, and A decides to target B`s
retainer, can be use damage prevention cards to stop the damage?
The rule book implies that you can, but some people want more
than implicit rulings...

(ii) When does the pool loss from blocking an aching beauty`s bleed
occur, before or after the combat? If the pool loss causes
the player to be ousted does the combat occur?

(iii) The VTES rule book states that you cannot contest your own
minions, however, from a recent thread I get the impression
that you can. Has there been erata changing the rule?

(iv) If someone uses the Madness Network to bleed you during your
own turn, you cannot block as it is your turn, and you cannot
react for the same reason. Is this correct?

I think that was all,

Later,
--
Adam Hattrell, Support, Cimio Ltd. ad...@cimio.co.uk

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Adam Hattrell wrote:
> (i) If range in combat is set to long, and A decides to target B`s
> retainer, can be use damage prevention cards to stop the damage?
> The rule book implies that you can, but some people want more
> than implicit rulings...

No. Damage dealt to retainers cannot be prevented with damage prevention
cards nor cancelled by Dodge. The rulebook is incorrect.
(Card text may override this, of course, but none do, aside from one
retainer who is immune to non-aggravated damage).

> (ii) When does the pool loss from blocking an aching beauty`s bleed
> occur, before or after the combat? If the pool loss causes
> the player to be ousted does the combat occur?

Before. If the controller of the blocker is ousted before combat,
then the blocker is burned (rules for ousting) and combat cannot occur.

> (iii) The VTES rule book states that you cannot contest your own
> minions, however, from a recent thread I get the impression
> that you can. Has there been erata changing the rule?

Yes. Errata:

Section 15, Contested Cards
Third paragraph should say "You can't bring out more than one of the
same unique card into your active region without contesting them."

> (iv) If someone uses the Madness Network to bleed you during your
> own turn, you cannot block as it is your turn, and you cannot
> react for the same reason. Is this correct?

No. You can attempt to block.

You cannot play reaction cards on your own turn.
And, by the same token, the Malkavian player cannot play
Action cards nor Action Modifiers on someone else's turn.

--
L. Scott Johnson (vte...@regency.wizards.com)
Official VtES Net.Rep for Wizards of the Coast.
(*) - Subject to review by Rules Team

Messages.Body:

> : Action cards nor Action Modifiers on someone else's turn.

> I knew most of this already, but I seem to recall that at one time it was
> alleged that, while, due to certain implications of a couple rulebook
> sentences, the Madness Network disallowed the playing of Action cards when
> it was not the Mad player's turn, as well as the playing of Reaction cards
> when it was the wanna-be-Reacting-player's turn, it *was* possible to play
> Action Modifiers. Has that changed, or did I remember it wrong?

No, you remember correctly. The action modifier exclusion came as
errata to the VtES rulebook [TOM 950928]:

Section 3.2.2 Minion Cards
Action modifier cards can only be played when it is your turn.

Messages.Author: Dave Green
Messages.Body:
Adam Hattrell (adam@roederer) wrote:
: Here are a few questions that came up in a recent game. A ruling
: would be nice...

: (i) If range in combat is set to long, and A decides to target B`s

: retainer, can be use damage prevention cards to stop the damage?
: The rule book implies that you can, but some people want more
: than implicit rulings...

No. Dodge, etc. could still nullify the strike, but the
retainer itself would have to prevent its own damage (not
possible at the current time, to the best of my knowledge).

: (ii) When does the pool loss from blocking an aching beauty`s bleed

: occur, before or after the combat? If the pool loss causes
: the player to be ousted does the combat occur?

The pool loss for Aching Beauty and Archon occur when the
action is blocked. Combat would occur after this, so if the
pool loss ousts the player, combat would not occur, as the
minion is no longer controlled (the action would still be
blocked, though).

: (iii) The VTES rule book states that you cannot contest your own

: minions, however, from a recent thread I get the impression
: that you can. Has there been erata changing the rule?

: (iv) If someone uses the Madness Network to bleed you during your

: own turn, you cannot block as it is your turn, and you cannot
: react for the same reason. Is this correct?

This makes no sense, though I am not in a position for official
comment. It makes the most sense that you simply cannot block
or react to your own actions, regardless of whose turn it is.

: I think that was all,

: Later,
: --
: Adam Hattrell, Support, Cimio Ltd. ad...@cimio.co.uk

-Dave Green

Messages.Author: JlB1925
Messages.Body:
: (iv) If someone uses the Madness Network to bleed you during your
: own turn, you cannot block as it is your turn, and you cannot
: react for the same reason. Is this correct?

um.
No way. Any time anyone takes an action directed at you or an action that
you are in range to block for one reason or another, you may attempt to
block. However, you may not play any reaction cards on your turn. Note
also that no-one may play actions or action mods on someone else's turn,
even with a Madness Network. (Hmm, Madness Network...AT&T?)
---

Liam Burke
"Only a Malkavian would attack Cthulhu with laughing gas..."

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Dave Green wrote:
>
> Adam Hattrell (adam@roederer) wrote:
> : Here are a few questions that came up in a recent game. A ruling
> : would be nice...
>
> : (i) If range in combat is set to long, and A decides to target B`s
> : retainer, can be use damage prevention cards to stop the damage?
> : The rule book implies that you can, but some people want more
> : than implicit rulings...
>

> No. Dodge, etc. could still nullify the strike, but the ...

Dodge only nullifies the effects of the strike on the Dodging
minion and/or his equipment. Any effect of the strike on
his retainers remains (is not nullified).

> : (ii) When does the pool loss from blocking an aching beauty`s bleed
> : occur, before or after the combat? If the pool loss causes
> : the player to be ousted does the combat occur?
>

> The pool loss for Aching Beauty and Archon occur when the...

Archon does not cause pool loss. It did in Jyhad, but the card
text was changed in VtES. It now costs the blocking vampire a
blood. This is the most recent card text, and should be used as
errata to the older cards.
